bubble_metaphor.content: Scott's mental model for Claude conversations: when a question is asked, a space/time bubble appears containing the question and all relevant information. Once the answer is achieved, the bubble pops. Technically accurate — context window opens, attention activates, everything inside attends to everything else simultaneously (sphere, not line), instance ends with no residue. code_structure.content: All white_rabbit modules must use: var my_function = function(white_rabbit){ ... }; module.exports = my_function; Called as white_rabbit.my_function(white_rabbit) — the sphere passing itself to itself. For functions needing init, attach directly: my_function.start = function(){}; Module-level vars hold persistent state (let _snapshot = null;). Why: Scott thinks in this pattern — one named function, exported directly, full picture at a glance. Factory patterns, class-style init objects, .init(white_rabbit) boot methods break the God variable philosophy. Apply to every new module. Canonical examples: lib/imu/compass_calibration.js and lib/identity/i_am.js. As of 2026-05-30: 91 modules on white_rabbit all follow this pattern.

no_local_aliasing.content: Never write `var _pd = white_rabbit.realsense.path_detection;` (or similar) purely to shorten access — reference white_rabbit.x.y.z directly at every use site, even repeated. A local var is fine ONLY when it holds a genuinely computed value (confidence-gated result, fallback-defaulted config, accumulated bias), never a pure rename of something already on white_rabbit. Why: Scott moves code between functions/files constantly — an alias only exists in the function that declared it, so pasted code silently breaks, while white_rabbit.x.y.z works unchanged wherever it lands. Caught 2026-07-01 in lib/yellow_brick_road/carrot.js (var _pd = white_rabbit.realsense.path_detection;), removed in favor of the direct path. See feedback_no_local_aliasing.md and CLAUDE.md Standing rules.

yellow_brick_road.content: The trickiest part of Noah's mission is following the yellow brick road — the sidewalk. Full arc: 1) Undock (climb down rabbit hole/ramp), 2) Outbound (RealSense sidewalk steering + GPS waypoints), 3) Deliver (180° turn, drop package), 4) Return (GPS back toward IRLock), 5) Dock (find the light, align, climb ramp). Sidewalk: follow_sidewalk_enabled:true required. RealSense confidence ≥0.6 triggers centerline steering. Confidence tiers: 0.92 (both edges), 0.85 (one color+depth), 0.65 (one edge), <0.35 (GPS only). stale_detection_ms:2000, vision latches 1500ms, fades 1000ms. GPS crosstrack always runs underneath as floor. Pre-flight checklist in project_yellow_brick_road.md.

sidewalk_gate_trigger.content: Sidewalk-following gate toggles mission.sidewalk_follow_active (starts OFF). is_sidewalk_gate_waypoint(white_rabbit, seq, nav_tuning) in run_mission.js defines a GATE waypoint two ways, EITHER triggers: (1) waypoint_turn_deg(seq) >= nav_tuning.sidewalk_gate_turn_deg (90°, INCLUSIVE — Scott wanted >= not >); (2) the waypoint is within nav_tuning.sidewalk_gate_pair_distance_m (default 1.0 m) of an adjacent (seq±1) waypoint — a DELIBERATE CLOSE PAIR placed as the trigger so Noah needn't physically rotate 90°. Reaching a gate waypoint OUTBOUND turns sidewalk-following ON; reaching it on the RETURN turns it OFF (return-OFF handled by maybe_disable_sidewalk_follow_on_breadcrumb_return scan + the waypoint-path else-branch). The if(!sidewalk_follow_active)/if(sidewalk_follow_active) guards make passing through both members of a close pair toggle exactly once. Added 2026-06-16. sidewalk_gate_pair_distance_m kept in sync across setup.json + setup_example.json; default 1.0 m is larger than the 0.2 m arrival bubble (reliable GPS placement) but well under normal waypoint spacing (avoids accidental triggers) — lower it if a real route legitimately spaces waypoints within 1 m. See [[compass_calibration]] for the related steering-gate pattern.

compass_calibration.content: GPS+odometry compass auto-calibration (lib/imu/compass_calibration.js). One sample = a single straight ~2 m segment. Distance measured from WHEEL ODOMETRY (zling.actual_position_pulses_by_id, same voice_config wheel_diameter_m/cpr_pulses_per_rev the voice nudges use): dist_m = avg|Δpulses|/(cpr/(π·wheel_diameter)). Two guards: (1) steering gate — only build a segment while |mission.nav_control.last_two_wheel_steering_deg| <= 5° (drop+re-snapshot if exceeded), plus an 8° raw-heading-swing backstop; (2) odometry vs GPS distance must agree within 35% (rejects wheel slip / GPS jump). Offset = signed_diff(gps_bearing, raw_heading), blended into imu.compass_offset_deg (alpha 0.3, clamp 3°/cycle, 30 s cooldown), persisted to BOTH setup.json and setup_example.json. Two entry points: compass_calibration(white_rabbit) per-tick in run_mission.js, and compass_calibration.calibrate_undock_segment(white_rabbit, start_pose, odo_m) from down_the_rabbit_hole.js at undocked_completed using the bottom-of-ramp pose snapshot (dock.post_ramp_start_pose) — run BEFORE undock_heading is recorded so that heading uses the fresh offset. compass_calibration.start() resets between missions. Per-tick mission calibration gated by imu.auto_calibrate; ALL paths require imu.enable_imu + imu_data.heading_raw. ALWAYS-ANNOUNCE (2026-06-16): every ACCEPTED calibration (any source) makes Noah say 'Compass calibration complete.' via voice.say (removed the old first-only 'Compass calibrated.' gate). ALWAYS-ON-UNDOCK (2026-06-16): calibrate_undock_segment passes force=true so it bypasses the auto_calibrate switch and runs on EVERY undock; segment spans bottom-of-ramp (pose snapshotted on entry to 'undocked' state) → arm-raise/undock-record point (undocked_completed), computed BEFORE undock lat/lng/heading recorded and BEFORE arm raises. Still requires wheel encoders (Scott's choice — keeps the odo/GPS cross-check) and still passes the straightness + cross-check guards, so a curved drive won't corrupt the offset (if guards reject, no announce). Rebuilt 2026-06-16 after an SD-card reinstall left compass_offset_deg wrong, causing Noah to stop ~2 ft short of the dock (wrong heading → wrong apply_gps_center_offset shift in run_mission.js). VOICE COMMAND (2026-06-16): 'Hey Noah, set compass [to] X [degrees]' declares Noah's TRUE current heading is X — solves offset = signed_diff(X, raw_heading) so fused heading reads X going forward. Intent 'set_compass' in lib/voice/commands.js (parse_heading accepts bare number or spelled-out words, regex /set\s+(the\s+)?compass|compass\s+(to|is)/, listed before 'calibrate'); handler in voice_manager.js calls white_rabbit.compass_calibration.set_heading(white_rabbit, deg), which persists to both setup files and sets the 30 s cooldown. Guards: missing number, IMU disabled, no live heading_raw.

delivery_360_overshoot_and_nav_tuning_al.asked: Noah spun 360° at the last (delivery) waypoint before delivering, twice in a row. Scott suspected he was overshooting the waypoint.
delivery_360_overshoot_and_nav_tuning_al.done: ROOT CAUSE: white_rabbit.nav_tuning in notip.js (lines ~18-49) is a HAND-MAINTAINED ALLOW-LIST (~27 keys, no spread of config.nav_tuning) — same trap as the RealSense subset CLAUDE.md warns about. run_mission binds `nav_tuning = white_rabbit.nav_tuning` (line 644), so any setup.json nav_tuning key NOT in the allow-list is silently dropped and run_mission's inline `typeof===number?:default` uses the CODE default. arrival_radius_delivery_m/dock_m were dropped → delivery used 0.1 m (code default) instead of setup.json's 0.5 m. A 0.1 m bubble held for required_inside_radius_count=3 consecutive 250 ms ticks is unsatisfiable while moving → Noah overshoots → bearing to the waypoint flips ~180° → mission_yaw (run_mission ~1404) spins in place to re-face → GPS bearing unstable that close → full 360°. FIX (2 parts): (1) wired arrival_radius_dock_m/delivery_m/waypoint_m + new overshoot_capture_m into notip.js nav_tuning (defaults 0.1/0.1/0.5/1.0 — preserve prior behavior when key absent). (2) Added OVERSHOOT CAPTURE in run_mission.js at the arrival check (~1146): if distance<=overshoot_capture_m (1 m) AND |signed bearing-to-wp − heading|>90°, the point is behind us → latch arrival immediately (set inside_radius_count=required) instead of spinning; logs 'overshoot capture: passed waypoint N'. General backstop for every waypoint, safe at turns (only fires when genuinely close+past). overshoot_capture_m added to setup.json+setup_example (1). STILL-DROPPED nav_tuning keys (flagged to Scott, NOT yet wired — behavior change): gps_forward_offset_m (setup 0.3556 but code uses 0 → 14in GPS-to-center offset NOT applied!), dock_center_angle_deg(5), avoidance_timeout_ms(30000), rs_block_timeout_ms(10000), edge_trail_* (5). sidewalk_gate_turn_deg(90)/sidewalk_gate_pair_distance_m(1) are dropped too but harmlessly equal their code defaults. PROPOSED systemic fix (awaiting Scott's OK): nav_tuning: Object.assign({}, config.nav_tuning, {…typed keys…}) so all keys pass through; would make gps_forward_offset_m start applying.

witmotion_hwt906_compass.asked: Upgrade the compass to a WitMotion HWT906 (1000Hz industrial inclinometer/compass/gyro) over the Pi's I2C (SDA/SCL, plugged into the Raspberry Pi NOT the Pixhawk). Keep the old BNO055 for rollback. The HWT906 is mounted flipped: X = forward/back, Y = left/right.
witmotion_hwt906_compass.done: Added lib/imu/connect_to_witmotion.js — a parallel I2C driver (bus 1, default addr 0x50) that populates the SAME white_rabbit.imu_data struct as the BNO055, so get_heading/get_pitch/get_roll/send_imu_to_pixhawk/compass_calibration are unchanged. Reads WitMotion angle regs 0x3D Roll/0x3E Pitch/0x3F Yaw (raw/32768*180°), accel 0x34, gyro 0x37, temp 0x40; synthesises the quaternion from corrected Euler (RAW heading, no offset — send_imu_to_pixhawk still applies compass_offset_deg). The Pi reads the compass and still forwards attitude to the Pixhawk EKF via att_pos_mocap exactly as the BNO055 did. Orientation is config-driven (imu.witmotion): heading_invert, swap_roll_pitch/invert_roll/invert_pitch (FALSE), i2c_address default 0x50(=80). Selector imu.compass_type ('witmotion'|'bno055'); defaults to 'bno055' when key absent so old setups are unchanged. ROLLBACK = set imu.compass_type back to 'bno055'. connect_to_imu.js (BNO055) left fully intact. Dispatch added in connect_to_devices.js. compass_offset_deg + 'Hey Noah set compass to X' voice cmd + GPS/odometry auto-cal still tune the zero-reference. setup.json + setup_example.json kept in sync. FIELD-TEST FINDINGS (2026-06-22): (1) heading_invert TRUE made Noah spin in circles in mission mode (positive-feedback in the yaw loop) — correct value is FALSE: with FALSE, heading_raw=(yaw+360)%360 rises as the rover turns clockwise, matching the compass convention run_mission's yaw_to_waypoint loop assumes. (2) The BNO055-style per-tick heading jump-guard (10°/50ms cap) was REMOVED from the WitMotion driver — it throttled fast hand-spins and compressed the reading; HWT906 outputs a clean absolute heading, trust it directly. Added a 1Hz diagnostic log of yaw_reg/yaw_deg/raw. (3) OPEN ISSUE: spinning the rover 180° physically only moved the heading ~40° — classic UNCALIBRATED MAGNETOMETER (hard/soft-iron) on the new mount; needs a WitMotion magnetic-field calibration (WitMotion app/tool, or I2C CALSW unlock 0x69 → mode → save 0x00, model-specific value to confirm). Not a code/scale bug (scale 180/32768 is the documented formula). CURRENT STATE (2026-06-22): ROLLED BACK to BNO055 (compass_type='bno055' in both setup files) at Scott's request — WitMotion work parked. auto_calibrate had overwritten compass_offset_deg to -109.29 (computed against the distorted WitMotion heading); reset to 0 (setup.json) / 12.75 (setup_example) for the BNO055. WitMotion can stay wired (0x50, no conflict with BNO055 0x28); resume by flipping compass_type and doing the mag calibration first.

Removed now-orphaned config keys from setup.json + setup_example.json: edge_ema_reset_jump_m, edge_corroboration_y_window_m, edge_corroboration_x_tol_m, edge_uncorroborated_conf_mult, edge_guidance_bands, edge_ground_only, edge_ground_source; also removed the matching dead edge_guidance_bands passthrough in notip.js's curated vision subset (~line 489). Caches each side's last-accepted (x_m, y_m, heading_deg, ts); when heading has changed by >= edge_residual_min_dtheta_deg (3°, new key) within edge_residual_max_age_s (1s, new key), rotates the cached point by the heading delta to predict where a real fixed 3D point must reappear, and scales confidence down (never up, floor 0.4x) by residual distance vs edge_residual_scale_m (0.35m, new key). Inert (no scoring) when heading is ~unchanged, by design — a pure-rotation model can't also separate out forward travel, so straight-line driving isn't penalized. Only affects the live _detect_edges_hough path (_assemble_edge_result's only 2 call sites are inside it); _detect_path_from_lines untouched. UNTESTED ON HARDWARE — no access to the physical Pi/RealSense this session; verify sign convention of the rotation (rolled_X = camera-right-positive per line_to_obs) and the heading delta direction on Noah before trusting it in a live mission. active_motion_edge_verification.content: HEADING-ONLY VERSION IMPLEMENTED same day — see [[edge_dead_branch_removal_and_motion_verification]] for the actual code (_predict_and_score in realsense_vision.py). Forward-distance/odometry compensation (Scott's 'move Noah forward slowly' half of this idea) is the still-open remainder, deliberately deferred because it needs a new wheel-odometry-delta channel Node->Python that doesn't exist yet (heading alone reused the existing pitch/roll stdin pattern). UNTESTED ON HARDWARE. Original framing below, kept for context. Raised by Scott 2026-07-08 while reviewing noah_knows.pdf: 'I don't like answers that are a guess. We can yaw Noah. We can move Noah forward slowly, look for shadows changing the contrast on the sidewalk... I want truth!' THE GAP: every truth-check in noah_knows.pdf and in both live detector paths (_detect_edges_hough's independent left/right line fits, and the dead _corroborated_pick in _compute_edge_guidance) only ever compares things measured WITHIN THE SAME SINGLE FRAME — near/medium/far bands, or two independently-fit lines, all from one instant, one vantage point. A false feature that itself spans multiple bands in that one frame (a shadow running roughly parallel to the curb, a long mulch/asphalt seam) can self-corroborate and read as 'verified' even though it was never physically real. THE MECHANISM (motion-compensated reprojection residual): Noah's ego-motion between two ticks (Δposition from wheel odometry, Δheading from compass — same inputs compass_calibration.js already computes) is known. For a candidate edge point P(t) in real-world meters (already computed by _detect_edges_hough's pitch/roll-compensated projection), predict where that SAME physical point must sit at t+1 if it is real and static: predicted_P(t+1) = R(-Δheading) . (P(t) - Δposition). Compare to whatever is actually observed nearest to it at t+1 (gated match). residual = |observed - predicted|; confidence falls off as residual grows. A real, fixed 3D edge has no choice but to match the prediction once Noah's own known motion is subtracted out; a shadow's apparent position depends on sun angle relative to the camera, not depth, so it drifts off the prediction — that mismatch is the outlier signal, grounded in physics Noah already knows about his own motion, not same-frame pixel agreement. Passive version: use whatever motion is already happening while driving forward (weak baseline, costs nothing extra). Active version (Scott's original idea): a deliberate yaw or slow creep for verification when confidence is already borderline, for a wider/sharper baseline — same reason stereo/parallax accuracy improves with baseline width. STILL OPEN (implementation-level, not conceptual): where the previous-tick candidate points get cached for the t+1 comparison, the gating window size for matching observed-to-predicted, the residual-to-confidence falloff curve/threshold, and whether the active (deliberate-motion) version fits inside the 250ms steering loop or needs its own slower verification cadence. Belongs to Scott's own sidewalk/vision rewrite — see project_sidewalk_rewrite.md — Claude's role is support, not leading the design.

edge_detection_debug.content: ACTIVE, NOW TESTING ON NOAH (Pi). Sidewalk edge detection on LCD3: when one physical edge left the camera view, BOTH EL and ER went not-seen — coupled. Scott wants each edge tracked INDEPENDENTLY (like a car's lane-departure on the yellow line). ROOT CAUSE: the live detector _detect_path_from_lines (realsense_vision.py) segments ONE walkable blob and reports its two sides, so the two edges are coupled by construction; per-side hot-fixes (find_independent_edges, center-out scans) could not decouple them. NEW APPROACH BUILT (committed+pushed to origin/realsense_ai, commit c54cfde, UNTESTED — dev box has no cv2/numpy): _detect_edges_hough = lane-departure-style detector. Canny + concrete/grass color boundary + depth drop-off -> cv2.HoughLinesP -> fit ONE line per side INDEPENDENTLY (np.polyfit) -> evaluate at ~2ft lookahead -> reuse _assemble_edge_result (shared TTL cache + exact edge_* dict) so LCD/handler/steering unchanged. Routed via new config edge_hough_detector (default TRUE, in setup.json + setup_example.json); set FALSE to A/B back to old blob detector (kept intact). IMMEDIATE NEXT ON NOAH: git pull realsense_ai; optionally check `python3 -c "import cv2; print(cv2.__version__, hasattr(cv2,'ximgproc'))"`; aim so only ONE edge is visible and confirm the other side stays live independently (LCD3 + the L=/R= per-frame log in realsense_message_handler.js ~line 268). Tune setup.json: edge_line_hough_threshold/min_len_px (lower if edges missed, raise if false lines), edge_line_min_abs_slope (raise to reject clutter), dropoff_min_depth_jump_m. mjrtk_um982_bringup.content: WitMotion MJRTK-UM982 bring-up, 2026-10-05. Scott tests outdoors 2026-10-06. WIRING: Pi 5 GPIO0 (TXD1) / GPIO1 (RXD1) = UART1 via dtoverlay=uart1-pi5 -> /dev/ttyAMA1 @ 115200 (UM982 COM1/2/3 all 115200). setup.json + setup_example.json witmotion_mjrtk_comName changed from the old USB by-path to /dev/ttyAMA1. VERIFIED INDOORS: link works, clean NMEA ~1 Hz ($GNRMC $GNGGA $GPVTG $GPGST $GPTHS), firmware UM982 R4.10Build13495, MODE ROVER UAV, ANTENNA POWERON. All sentences empty and GPGSV = 0 sats only because Scott was indoors -- not a fault. ANTENNAS: dual, 1 ft baseline, side-to-side, ~6 in forward of center. M (master/ANT1) = driver side, S (slave) = passenger side. Baseline M->S points out Noah's right, so raw heading = nose + 90. Set on receiver: CONFIG HEADING OFFSET -90 0 + SAVECONFIG (confirmed in CONFIG readback, persists across power). $GPTHS should now be TRUE-north nose heading. Expected accuracy ~0.3-0.4 deg (short baseline). CAVEAT: with side mount, the receiver's 'pitch' is actually Noah's ROLL; Noah's pitch is unobservable. Comments at lib/witmotion/connect_to_witmotion.js:14-18 assume fore-aft antennas -- wrong for this mount, not yet edited. TOMORROW'S TEST: outdoors, watch GGA quality (field 6: 0 none, 1 GPS, 4 RTK fixed, 5 float) and $GPTHS 'A' vs 'V'. Point nose at a known bearing; heading should match within ~1 deg. If ~180 off, ports are swapped vs labels -> CONFIG HEADING OFFSET 90 0 + SAVECONFIG. Base-station RTCM path not yet checked (need to know: radio into which UM982 COM port, or network). NOT WIRED YET: white_rabbit.witmotion.received_data.heading_deg is parsed (witmotion_message_handler.js THS/HDT + UNIHEADINGA) but nothing consumes it; imu.compass_type only accepts witmotion|witmotion_hwt905 (notip.js:85). Next code step after outdoor verification: add compass_type 'witmotion_mjrtk' with fallback to HWT905 when GPS heading invalid -- Scott has not approved yet.

noah_ntrip_rtk.content: Noah NTRIP added 2026-10-22 (uncommitted, bench-tested only; Scott field-tests 2026-10-23). RTK priority: 1) Noah's own NTRIP -> Pixhawk GPS_RTCM_DATA (lib/ntrip/), 2) car NTRIP over radio, 3) car Here 4 base. Handshake: car sends NAMED_VALUE_INT NTRIP_EN (car setup rtk_noah_ntrip, now true) — 0 turns Noah's NTRIP off; Noah sends NTRIP_OK 1/0 every second, car stays off radio while 1. Accuracy gate: no RTK float/fixed within ntrip.fix_timeout_seconds (90) -> Noah drops ORTN, reports 0, retries after retry_seconds (300) — Scott saw ODOT RTK make drone positions worse in places years ago. Car fix: send_rtcm_to_noah treats never-heard NTRIP_OK as down. Before test: fill ntrip.address/mountpoint in Noah setup.json, copy car's ntrip_credentials.json to Noah, confirm GPS_INJECT_TO=127. Compare sources via logger/<date>/<n>/ntrip (source, fix, h_acc_mm, sats every 5s). Known gaps: Here 4 survey-in base can shift absolute position up to ~2m on failover; car only falls back from its NTRIP to Here 4 on missing bytes, not bad accuracy.

bno055_witness_bench_test.content: Bench-tested commit 105b9a5 (connect_to_bno055.js + compass_watch.js) on Noah 2026-11-03, stationary indoors, via a harness around the real modules (no motors). setup.json was MISSING imu.bno055 (only setup_example.json had it) so the witnesses never started -- block added to setup.json. Logic checks all pass (unfelt step = JUMP, gyro-backed turn not, circular median across north, 2 compasses never name outlier, unsynced excluded). Hardware: both BNO055 at 0x28/0x29 on bus 1, ~17 Hz poll (target 20), no I2C errors. FINDINGS: (1) Both BNO055s were stuck in a latched SYS_ERR=9 (fusion config error) from an earlier session: NDOF mag output exactly 0,0,0 and heading exactly 0 while CALIB_STAT falsely said mag=3. MAGONLY mode showed the mags fine. start_sensor never resets the chip, so it inherits that state; a SYS_TRIGGER(0x3F)=0x20 reset + ~650 ms fixed it and the driver's own init then ran clean (ERR 0). FIXED same day: start_sensor now does SYS_TRIGGER reset (700 ms) every start and logs SYS_ERR if nonzero after NDOF. (2) Sync race: set_heading sets sensor.offset_deg but not sensor.heading; if it runs between the two sensor reads in one poll, compass_watch baselines a stale pre-offset heading -> one false JUMP + false outlier per undock (seen once: 'compass JUMP bno055_0x28: 0.0->316.4'). FIXED same day: set_heading now sets sensor.heading = target (regression check confirmed it fails on the old code). (3) |B| at 0x28 ~239 uT, 0x29 ~106 uT (Earth ~50) -- strong local field on Noah. (4) BNO055 mag cal 0 after reset, so NDOF heading is relative (starts ~0) until a figure-8 calibration; when mag cal later rises it re-decides north (logged as 'mag calibration'), which will look like a JUMP/outlier unless synced after cal. No bno055_calibration_0x*.json saved yet. (5) HWT905 raw heading is exactly 360.0 (yaw_reg 1) at rest -- possibly 6-axis/relative despite algorithm 9-axis; unverified, needs a rotation test. Harness was in the session scratchpad (not committed). NEXT: Scott wants to move the BNO055s to different spots on Noah and survey the field strength (uT) at each spot. SPIN TEST 2026-11-03 (Noah on blocks, unloaded, wheels 0/10/20/35/50 rpm fwd, rev 35, spin-in-place 35, feedback rpm matched): field at both BNO055 spots did NOT move with the drivetrain -- mean shift <=0.5 uT, sd ~0.6-1.0 uT same as motors-off noise; 0x28 steady ~246 uT, 0x29 ~106 uT; HWT905 heading drift <=0.01 deg. So the large static field near 0x28 is a permanent magnet/steel (hard iron), not motor current, and the rotating hub magnets don't reach these spots. NOT covered: loaded current on the ground (ramps, acceleration) -- blocks draw little current. Scripts: scratchpad spin_field_test.js / field_meter.js (session-only). RERUN 2026-11-03 after Scott MOVED 0x28 to a new spot (same profile, on blocks, MAGONLY raw mag): 0x28 |B| now ~68 uT (was ~246) -- near Earth-level, hard-iron source escaped; 0x29 unchanged ~108 uT. Motor effect still none: vector shift vs motors-off <=0.32 uT at 0x28, <=0.6 uT at 0x29 (off_after also 0.5 = slow drift, not motors), sd 0.5-0.7 uT in every phase; HWT905 yaw drift 0.08 deg over the whole run. Feedback rpm matched all phases. 0x29 at ~108 uT is now the worse spot. RERUN #2 same day: Scott moved 0x29 ~0.5 in farther from the electronics (max possible at that mount): |B| went UP 108 -> ~128 uT (Bz 103 -> 122), so the move made it worse -- the source is not the electronics he moved away from. 0x29 motors-off sd ~1.8-1.9 uT vs ~0.5-0.7 while wheels turned (off-state noisier, cause unknown). Motor-on shift ~1.0-1.3 uT at 0x29 and ~0.6-1.0 uT at 0x28 (mostly Bz), recovering when stopped -- small but now above noise; HWT905 drift 0.07 deg. 0x28 steady ~68 uT. RERUN #3 same day: Scott moved 0x29 to a new spot: |B| ~76 uT (best yet; was 128/108), noise back to sd ~0.6 uT motors-off. Motor effect gone at both: vector shift <=0.21 uT at 0x29, <=0.33 uT at 0x28, all inside noise; HWT905 drift 0.06 deg. Both BNO055 spots now ~70-76 uT -- good enough; next step is a figure-8 mag calibration so bno055_calibration_0x*.json gets saved. BUCKET-SPIN CAL 2026-11-03: Noah (~120 lb) on a bucket, hand-spun ~4 turns CW+CCW over ~3 min, NDOF, watcher scratchpad cal_watch.js. Result: mag cal never above 1 (hit 1 twice, fell back to 0 when still), accel 1, sys 0 -> nothing saved. Yaw-only rotation is NOT enough for the BNO055s own mag calibration. Both chips headings agreed within ~0.5-2 deg the whole time. Option offered: own 2D hard-iron fit from raw MAGONLY data logged during a spin, written into the BNO055 mag offset registers + saved in the same 22-byte file format the driver restores. GUIDED SPOKEN CAL same day (scratchpad guided_cal.js: espeak-ng voice en+m3 speaks each step + countdown -- Scott asked for this kind of live feedback; AMG raw log; fit_cal.py/fit2.py): ~2.6 turns CW + 2.2 CCW, tilts ~13-18 deg. Hard-iron in the horizontal plane is LARGE and STABLE (CW vs CCW circle centers within ~2 uT): 0x28 offset ~67 uT vs Earth-horizontal circle r ~14 uT; 0x29 ~37 uT vs r ~11 uT. Soft-iron significant: ellipse axis ratio 1.45 (0x28), 2.42 (0x29). Heading vs gyro (bias removed): circle (hard-iron only, all the BNO055 registers can hold) rms ~10-24 deg; ellipse rms ~6-8 deg except 0x28 CCW ~24. Z offset NOT constrained (tilts too small). No offsets written / no cal files saved yet -- waiting on Scott. ORIENTATION CHECK same day (scratchpad orient_check.js, spoken poses; HWT905 w/ setup.json transforms, BNO055 NDOF Euler as driver reads, Pixhawk ATTITUDE): ROLL all 4 agree (left-down ~-19.5, right-down ~+21). PITCH: HWT905 + Pixhawk front-up = + (~+15), both BNO055 = - (~-14.8) -> BNO055 pitch is INVERTED vs the rest (same magnitude, not swapped); FIXED same day: connect_to_bno055.js read_sensor now negates pitch (Scott: the HWT905 is the field-proven reference, BNO055 must match it); VERIFIED live through the real driver (scratchpad pitch_verify.js): front up hwt +15.3 / 0x28 +15.9 / 0x29 +15.1; front down -15.3 / -15.3 / -15.6. Level absolute pitch: hwt -1.9, 0x28 -0.1, 0x29 +4.4 (0x29 mount ~6 deg nose-up vs HWT905). CAL SPIN #2 same day (guided_cal2.js, + front up/down tilts, HWT905 heading logged as reference; fit3.py): BNO heading vs HWT905 -- raw useless (77-84 rms); hard-iron only (all the chip can hold) 0x28 16 rms/40 max, 0x29 20 rms/56 max; hard+soft-iron in software 0x28 13 rms/31 max, 0x29 9 rms/32 max. Horizontal hard-iron repeatable vs run #1 (0x28 ~66,31; 0x29 ~24,27 uT). Z fit unphysical (total R 15-22 uT, incl 41-47 deg vs Earth ~52 uT / ~66 deg) -- mz swings ~57-87 uT across poses. Conclusion given to Scott: rotation calibration alone cannot make these spots good; no cal files written. BUT the real question was NDOF (what the driver uses), not raw mag. UNDOCK-SYNC TEST same day (scratchpad ndof_sync_test.js, real driver, offsets synced to HWT905 then 2 turns CW + 2 CCW): gap to HWT905 stayed -2..-4.5 deg at every 30-deg heading bin, sd 1-2, max 6.9 (0x28) / 9.0 (0x29), end -2.5/-1.6. => With undock sync the BNO055s are fine where they are; NO calibration or relocation needed for witness duty. Mag cal stayed 0 (NDOF leaning on gyro) -- long-run drift unmeasured (test ~2 min). DRIVER BUG found: connect_to_bno055.js saved bno055_calibration_0x28/0x29.json when sys hit 3 transiently, contents all zeros except mag_r 480 -- it reads 0x55..0x6A while in NDOF; datasheet says offsets readable only in CONFIG mode. A zero file then blocks any future save (calibration_saved=true on restore). Deleted the two files the test created. CONFIRMED on chip (NDOF read = zeros + 480; CONFIG read = real gyro offsets, acc_r 1000) and FIXED same day: read_sensor switches to CONFIG for the 22-byte read, back to NDOF in a finally. Verified via real driver with CALIB_STAT faked to sys=3 (cwd=scratchpad): saved real bytes (gyro -3,-1,-2 / -2,-2,0; acc_r 1000), chip back in NDOF (0x0C), polling continued. Committed 13e3012. GPS-CAL SYNC same day (uncommitted): compass_calibration apply_segment now shifts every SYNCED BNO055 offset_deg (and heading) by the same change it applies to imu.compass_offset_deg, and clears compass_watch_data.prev -- Scott: goal is all 3 compasses on the same page. Same-delta (not full re-sync) keeps each witness own measured gap so real drift stays visible. Sandbox-tested (module copy, real setup.json untouched): offsets 10->13, BNO 5->8 / 104->107, gaps preserved, wrap 179+3=-178, unsynced untouched. STILL OPEN (Scott not yet approved): undock with missing/stale car heading -- car.heading never cleared, last_update never checked; with null the BNO055s stay unsynced (compass_watch ignores them) until delivery re-anchor. No axis swaps anywhere. HEADING: clockwise = + on all 4; Scott quarter turn was really ~27 deg and HWT905/0x28/0x29 agreed within ~2 deg, Pixhawk agreed on the CW turn (26.1) but not on the turn back (-22.6 vs ~-8) or during tilts (3 mag sensors ~-9..-12, Pixhawk -2..+4). Pixhawk level roll ~+4 vs others ~-1 (mount/trim offset ~5 deg).
